assertions.name: hypA_symbolic_and_numeric_verdicts_agree
assertions.source: The probe computes rung-2 and Hyp-A's prediction as rational functions in q and simplifies the difference; it also evaluates both at q₀ to 50 dps. The symbolic verdict (diff == 0 → False) and the numerical one (relative gap 384.921 < 1e-40 → False) must agree, or the resolution is a simplification artefact rather than a result.

assertions.name: hbar_q_matches_its_definition
assertions.source: The auxiliary scan's own 'trivially' entry: (1 − q⁻¹)³ − ℏ_q³ must simplify to exactly 0, so ℏ_q is (q−1)/q as the rung-2 form assumes.

description: Definitive test of Hyp-A: does the rung 2 form ℏ_q³/[2]_q equal (3-strand Markov trace at identity) / dim_q(V_1)? Symbolic check using QOU Markov-trace convention tr_M(1 ∈ H_n) = z^(n-1), z = 1/(√q+1/√q). Hyp-A confirmed iff the difference simplifies to 0.

data.hypothesis: Hyp-A: rung_2 = tr_M(1 ∈ H_3) / dim_q(V_1) = z² / [2]_q
data.implications: Hyp-A as literally stated (tr_M(1 ∈ H_3) / dim_q(V_1)) does NOT yield the rung-2 form. Possible refinements: (a) 'Markov trace at identity' may need a different interpretation (e.g. 3-cycle braid trace); (b) /[2]_q may still be dim_q(V_1), but the ℏ_q³ numerator's categorical source is OPEN; (c) Hyp-B (Wenzl p_3) and Hyp-C (Kauffman bracket) remain untested.
